description_full: Lands' End, Inc. operates as a digital retailer of apparel, swimwear, outerwear, accessories, footwear, home products, and uniforms in the United States, Europe, and internationally. The company operates through U.S. eCommerce, Europe eCommerce, Outfitters, Third Party, Licensing, and Retail segments. It also sells uniform and logo apparel to businesses and their employees, and student households; and earns royalties on the use of Lands' End trademark. The company sells its products through its e-commerce websites and company operated stores, as well as through third party distribution channels under the Lands' End, Lands' End Lighthouse, Squall, Tugless Tank, Drifter, Outrigger, Marinac, Wanderweight, Beach Living, Supima, No-Gape, Anyweather, Waveshaper, Starfish, Little Black Suit, Iron Knees, Hyde Park, Year'Rounder, ClassMate, Willis & Geiger, and ThermaCheck brands. Lands' End, Inc. was founded in 1963 and is headquartered in Dodgeville, Wisconsin.

financial_summary: Lands' End, Inc. is a micro-cap consumer cyclical business with a $276M market cap on $1.2B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -9% over the past three years and -2% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 5% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 43%.

The business throws off $20M in free cash flow — roughly 2 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 9.01× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.8× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and thin 1.2× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 72% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.5× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
